notes:
Summary: Zenvera is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a multi-tenant inference platform powering real-time personalization + support chat. Primary ask: strict throughput guarantees and hard latency SLOs under reserved capacity with clear noisy-neighbor protections. They need a commercial offer that maps reserved GPUs to guaranteed QPS and per-route concurrency caps.

Key technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: low-latency chat (p95 target <= 90ms typical), embeddings batch windows (throughput up to 1.2k reqs/min), reranking (p95 <= 120ms).
- Traffic shaping: per-route quotas, token-based rate-limiting, priority lanes for latency-sensitive routes, burst bucket for short spikes.
- Tenant isolation: strict VM/GPU tenancy or soft isolation w/ enforced QoS; want ability to pin VIP customers to dedicated lanes.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: automatic detection of heavy batch jobs + backpressure, per-tenant concurrency caps, scheduler-level priority weights, and optional preemption for low-priority background jobs.
- Reserved GPU planning: prefer 8-12 H100 equiv reserved for initial commit, with clear burst policy to scale + ephemeral padding for day-of-week peaks. Need pricing that separates reserved baseline vs burst unit costs.
- SLA & SLOs: uptime SLA (99.9%), latency SLOs per-route (p95/p99 buckets) with defined credit formula; on-call escalation contact + quarterly performance review.

POC observations and call quotes:
- "We can tolerate some throughput variance but tail latency kills conversions" — CTO (M. Alvarez).
- Night 3 POC: a single tenant embedding job pushed p99 above 2s; proposed Redwood mitigations: priority lanes + preemptible batch slots.
- SE notes: need per-route token accounting visible in Console (token-level cost & latency breakdown) and alerting on delta from baseline.

Commercial/negotiation points under review:
- Binding throughput guarantee vs committed GPU units — Zenvera wants SLA language mapping reserved GPUs to min sustained QPS and latency targets.
- Credits for missed latency SLOs; cap on credits; sample calculation requested by legal.
- Data residency: logs/audits must remain in AWS us-east-1; retention configurable per-route.

Open items / ask from Redwood:
- Provide SOW template for Reserved Capacity that includes per-route SLO table + per-tenant priority lane design.
- Run full POC load that replicates their peak: 1.2k RPM embeddings bursts, sustained 200 qps chat, mixed rerank spikes.
- Clarify fallback behavior when reserved pool exhausted (auto-fallback to hosted variants? throttling?).

CRM-style shorthand next steps:
- AE (Evan) to push SOW draft by 2026-03-08.
- SE (Priya) to propose specific priority-lane config (routes, concurrency caps, preemption rules) by 2026-03-12.
- Legal to get sample SLA credit calc from Redwood finance; blocker: Zenvera legal needs data residency language.

Stated blockers: pending legal review of SLO credit calc; unclear cost model for reserved vs burst GPU units; need explicit per-route logging retention policy.
